subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the Design Assignment, what is a 'design brief'?
options: A set of requirements outlining the design problem to be solved
A finished piece of artwork submitted for marking
A written evaluation of another artist's work
A random collection of unrelated sketches
questions.explain: A design brief states the problem, purpose and requirements that the candidate's design must respond to.

questions.q: The specific group of people a design is intended for is known as the:
options: Target audience
Examination board
Preparatory period
Colour palette
questions.explain: The target audience is the group whose needs and tastes the design must suit.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical constraint that a design brief might specify?
options: The required size or format of the design
The candidate's personal opinion of the tutor
The weather on the day of the exam
The marks awarded to other candidates
questions.explain: Briefs commonly set constraints such as size, format, materials, function or audience that shape the design.

questions.q: Quick, rough preliminary sketches used to explore many possible ideas are called:
options: Thumbnail sketches
Final outcomes
Mount boards
Contact sheets
questions.explain: Thumbnail sketches let a designer rapidly generate and compare a range of ideas early on.

questions.q: A small trial version of a design, made to test how it will look or work, is best described as a:
options: Mock-up
Design brief
Target audience
Signature
questions.explain: A mock-up (or maquette) is a trial model used to test a design before producing the final version.

questions.q: In the Design Assignment, the completed, resolved piece submitted at the end is the:
options: Final design outcome
Initial brief
Preliminary thumbnail
Mood board
questions.explain: The final design outcome is the resolved solution that answers the brief.

questions.q: Written notes added to developmental work to explain the designer's thinking are called:
options: Annotation
Perspective
Composition
Symmetry
questions.explain: Annotation records the decisions and reasoning behind the development of a design.

questions.q: Why is it important to analyse the target audience before beginning to design?
options: So the design is appropriate and appealing to the people it is meant for
So the design takes the longest possible time to make
So the design can ignore the requirements of the brief
So the design uses only one colour
questions.explain: Understanding the audience ensures the design communicates effectively and suits their needs and tastes.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of identifying the constraints stated in a design brief?
options: To guide and focus realistic design decisions
To make the brief impossible to complete
To replace the need for any research
To decide another candidate's grade
questions.explain: Constraints such as size, materials and function keep the design practical and on-task.

questions.q: Why is producing several different idea options usually better than committing to a single idea straight away?
options: It allows a range of possibilities to be explored and compared before choosing
It guarantees the first idea is always used
It removes the need to respond to the brief
It hides the designer's development process
questions.explain: Exploring several options encourages richer development and a more informed final choice.

questions.q: How does annotating developmental work strengthen a Design Assignment?
options: It explains the reasoning and decisions behind the design's development
It increases the physical size of the artwork
It replaces the need for any drawings
It copies the brief word for word
questions.explain: Annotation makes the designer's thinking and choices visible to the examiner.

questions.q: Why might a candidate experiment with a variety of media and techniques while developing a design?
options: To discover which are most effective for communicating the design
To avoid making any decisions
To ensure the work cannot be assessed
To make the design match a friend's work
questions.explain: Experimenting helps identify the media and techniques best suited to the design's purpose.

questions.q: In design work, what does it mean for an outcome to be 'fit for purpose'?
options: It successfully meets the requirements and function set out in the brief
It is simply the largest piece produced
It uses the most expensive materials available
It ignores the intended audience
questions.explain: A fit-for-purpose design does the job the brief asked for, for its intended audience.

questions.q: Why does a designer refine a chosen idea before producing the final design?
options: To improve and resolve its quality so it fully answers the brief
To make the idea deliberately less clear
To avoid selecting any single idea
To reduce the number of marks available
questions.explain: Refinement resolves details and problems so the final outcome is polished and effective.

questions.q: Why is careful presentation of the final design important in the Design Assignment?
options: It shows the resolved outcome clearly and communicates the design effectively
It hides the development stages from the examiner
It removes the need to meet the brief
It makes the work impossible to display
questions.explain: Good presentation lets the final outcome communicate its purpose to the audience and examiner.

questions.q: A brief asks for a poster advertising a music festival aimed at teenagers. What is the most appropriate first step?
options: Identify the audience and the brief's requirements before generating ideas
Immediately produce the final printed poster with no planning
Design for retired adults instead of teenagers
Copy an existing festival poster without changes
questions.explain: Responding to a brief begins with understanding its audience, purpose and requirements.

questions.q: A candidate has drawn only one logo idea, and their teacher advises them to 'develop solutions'. What should they do next?
options: Create several variations and alternative ideas to explore possibilities
Submit the single idea unchanged as the final design
Delete the idea and start an unrelated project
Copy the teacher's own design exactly
questions.explain: Developing solutions means generating and testing a range of ideas rather than settling on one.

questions.q: A candidate finds their detailed logo becomes an unreadable blur when printed very small. Applying refinement, what is the best response?
options: Simplify the design so it remains clear at small sizes
Add even more fine detail to the logo
Ignore the problem and submit it anyway
Change the target audience to avoid the issue
questions.explain: Refining a design to remain legible at its intended size makes it fit for purpose.

questions.q: For a brief to design product packaging, which final presentation would best demonstrate that the design is fit for purpose?
options: A 3D mock-up showing how the packaging folds and functions
A single unlabelled colour swatch
A written list of the candidate's favourite artists
A blank sheet the same size as the brief
questions.explain: A working 3D mock-up shows the packaging performing its intended function for the audience.

questions.q: A design brief specifies that the outcome must be A3 portrait and use only two colours. During development, a candidate wants to use five colours across a landscape format. What should they do?
options: Keep within the brief's stated format and colour constraints
Ignore the brief and follow personal preference
Ask a classmate to change the brief
Abandon the assignment entirely
questions.explain: Responding to a brief means working within its stated constraints such as format and colour.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Art & Design (0400) syllabus; Component 2: Design Assignment
